newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Union Miniere stake re-placed overnight - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Union Miniere stake re-placed overnight - dealers.

text.p: Bourse trade in Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere was halted in the wake of an overnight private placement on Union Miniere shares, traders said on Wednesday.
They said the overall transaction had been worth 21 billion Belgian francs.

Dealers said about a third of the total, or 9.8 percent of Union Miniere's capital, had been re-placed already overnight. "It was a placement by Societe Generale via Merill Lynch at 3,400 francs per share," a trader said.
Trade in Union Miniere shares was halted at 1009 a.m. (0809 GMT) by the Brussels bourse. Before the suspension, UM had fallen 335 francs, or nine percent, to 3,410 francs.
Dealers said the fall was the result of sales by those who had taken part in the overnight placement.

Societe Generale de Belgique SA, the Belgian holding company, later said it sold a 24 percent stake in Union Miniere to a banking syndicate, which would place the shares with Belgian and international institutional investors.
The sale raised about 20 billion francs. SGB added it would book a capital gain of about 12 billion francs on the operation.
After the news Union Miniere was indicated at 3,450 francs.
A Brussels bourse spokeswoman said trade in Union Miniere shares would resume at 1130 a.m (0930 GMT).
